text:
The Rangers won 4-1, but the chance quality says Tampa Bay had the better of it: TBL out-attempted New York 57 to 43, edged expected goals 2.66 to 2.54, and would win 53 percent of simulated replays of every shot. What swung it was Alexis Lafrenière, who scored twice in the first period on chances worth 19 and 2 percent, the second of them a long shot that found its way in at 12:47 to make it 2-0. Zemgus Girgensons answered late in the period, but Tampa never caught up.

Dylan Garand did the rest. He faced 26 shots worth 2.66 expected goals and let in one, about 1.7 goals better than an average goalie would have managed. Andrei Vasilevskiy allowed three on 2.5 expected, so he was a touch below par, though the goals were not all his fault. Will Cuylle tipped one in with seven seconds left in the second period to make it 3-1, a goal that carried only an 8 percent chance and put the game out of easy reach.

Tampa's best stretch came in the second, when it outchanced New York 1.14 to 0.85, but it turned that edge into nothing. The Rangers tightened in the third, holding a 0.78 to 0.52 advantage, and Mika Zibanejad sealed it with a shorthanded goal at 17:16 on a 3 percent chance. Neither power play converted in four tries. It was the second win over Tampa Bay in two weeks, after a 5-1 result on Oct. 1.
